title: The verifier's spoiled-ballot openings under definition version 7 with a fixed electorate (opening version 3, without an author panel): definitions, clocks, boards and pinned panels, with the rows 2.3 and 6.2 and the report's openings
generator: packages/crypto/scripts/verifier-openings-v3-vectors.py, from verifier-ballots-v4-vectors.py, verifier-ceremony-vectors.py, spoiled-opening-v3-vectors.py and verifier-openings-vectors.py (independent Python implementations); the ballot records are verifier-ballots-v4-definition-v7.json's

cases.description: Definition version 7 under a fixed electorate without an author panel; close falls in period 2, so s_S is at least 3. The cell-0 ballot in segment 0 (counted whatever s_S is) and the tier-2 ballot in segment 4 (counted only if s_S ≥ 4); an honest opening in segment 3 (early); in segment 5 an opening of every check failure (opening-cell for cell 3, the first past the partition; opening-shape twice, for a missing seat and for an author half the poll has no panel for; opening-ciphertext for seat 2's ciphertext bound to the author panel), one that doesn't decode, one labelled version 2, an honest one, one of three picks in question 1 (outside at question 1), and two that re-use one ballot's (v_j, r_j) under other share hashes: the segment-0 ballot's (cast) and the segment-4 ballot's (undecided); in segment 6 a byte-identical copy of the honest one and of the stray one, and in segment 7 a third copy of the honest one (repeats, each of the first). The honest openings above the floor may still be early or late once s_S is known, so 6.2 is unverifiable.

Every opening breaks a rule the floor decides: an honest one in segment 3 (early), one re-using the segment-0 ballot's commitment (cast), one failing opening-vss, and a copy of the cast one (repeat). 6.2 fails at the first, opening-early.
The first settled opening is labelled version 2, which a profile pinning version 3 doesn't read: 6.2 fails with decode and profile-mismatch.
Only honest openings above the floor, opening no ballot on the copy: undecided until s_S is known, so 6.2 is unverifiable.
An opening that re-uses the commitment of the tier-2 ballot in segment 4, above the floor: whether that ballot is counted needs s_S, so no break is reported and 6.2 is unverifiable.
The same opening with the tier-2 ballot in segment 3, the floor itself: counted whatever s_S is, so the opening is cast and 6.2 fails.

Definition version 7 under a fixed electorate, with an opening in segment 5 made honestly for the same election read as version 6 (its version-6 hash, in the core and every ciphertext's associated data): it is opening-stray, so 6.2 fails.
